# sokkel-ui

> A shared React component library: one set of tokens and themes, Base UI primitives, and the patterns apps are built from (frame, layout, forms, tables, chat, files, media players, dashboards), with charts, maps, graphs, terminals and the music and video app parts in add-on packages. Apps install the packages and never copy from them, so one fix in the library reaches every app at its next version. Before building any UI part in an app, look it up in the component index.

## Packages

All six are published to GitHub Packages and released together at one version.

- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui` (core): the tokens and themes, the primitives and every pattern without an engine of its own. Every app installs it.
- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-charts`: `Chart` and its kinds on ECharts, and the dashboard's chart panels.
- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-maps`: `MapView` on maplibre, with its layers, legends, popups and basemaps.
- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-graph`: the graphs and the graph editor on React Flow, laid out by elk.
- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-terminal`: terminals on xterm.js: `TerminalView`, an interactive terminal whose connection the app owns, and `Terminal`, commands and their output.
- `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-media`: the music and video app parts: `MediaBar` (the player along the foot of a screen) and its fullscreen view, `TrackList`, `MediaCard`, `Artwork` (a cover, or one drawn from a seed), `useMediaSession` (media keys and the lock screen) and `hlsSource` (an HTTP live stream for `VideoPlayer`'s `source`, through hls.js, an optional peer the app installs). The players chat uses, `AudioPlayer` and `VideoPlayer`, and `SoundVisualizer` stay in the core.

## Install and import

The scope points at the registry in the app's `.npmrc` (`@winterop-com:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`, with a token that can read packages). Install the core, and an add-on only when the app draws charts, maps, graphs or terminals or plays music or video, all at the same version:

```
bun add @winterop-com/sokkel-ui @winterop-com/sokkel-ui-charts
bun add -d tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```

A library only some parts need is an optional peer dependency the app installs itself, and the app's build fails to resolve it until it does: `Markdown`, `AssistantReply` and `MessageComposer` need `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `rehype-raw`, `rehype-sanitize`, `shiki`, `mermaid`, `katex`, `remark-math` and `rehype-katex`; `Code` and the parts that show code need `shiki`; `SchemaForm` and `schema/validate` need `ajv` and `ajv-formats`; `CodeEditor` needs CodeMirror (`@codemirror/*`, `@lezer/highlight`), `ajv` and `ajv-formats`; `DateField`, `DateTimeField`, `dashboard/TimeRange` and `primitives/calendar` need `react-day-picker`; the calendar views, `board/BoardCard` and `DueText` need `date-fns`; `primitives/carousel`, `primitives/sonner`, `primitives/input-otp`, `primitives/resizable`, `primitives/questionnaire` and `primitives/message-scroller` need `embla-carousel-react`, `sonner`, `input-otp`, `react-resizable-panels` and `@shadcn/react`; `hlsSource` needs `hls.js`. The README's table lists them. Each part loads its library on first use where it can (maplibre, ECharts and the chart kinds, ajv, the calendar, Shiki, KaTeX, Mermaid), so a page carries none of it until it draws the part; `loadMapEngine`, `loadSchemaChecks` and `loadMath` fetch one ahead.

The app runs Tailwind CSS 4.1 or later itself. Each package's `styles.css` is Tailwind source, not finished CSS, so it must be `@import`ed in the same stylesheet as the core's `styles.css`, after it; importing it from JavaScript produces nothing. A theme other than tidevann, the base theme, needs its file, `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/themes/<name>.css`, imported too, and is set on `<html data-theme="<name>">` (`.dark` picks dark mode):

```css
/* app.css, imported once from the entry */
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/styles.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-charts/styles.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/themes/paper.css';
```

Every add-on's styles go the same way, after the core's: `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-maps/styles.css`, `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-graph/styles.css`, `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-terminal/styles.css` and `@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-media/styles.css`.

An app that offers every theme (a theme picker in its settings) imports them all at once instead, about 9 kB gzipped for all ten, and `ThemePicker` then shows each one:

```css
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/styles.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/themes.css';
```

The themes are tidevann (the base theme, in `styles.css`, worn with no `data-theme`), amber, paper, contrast, tokyo, vinyl, cassette, neon, ocean, indigo and terminal.

`styles.css` points Tailwind at every core module, so the CSS carries classes of components the app never imports (49 kB gzipped for a forms page). An app that wants only what it uses imports `styles-base.css` instead, then one line per module it imports, from any package: that module's list of sources, `sources/<module>.css` under the name the module is imported by. A list covers the module and every module it draws on, and an add-on's list brings the core lists it needs, so on this path it replaces the add-on's `styles.css` (the same forms page: 20 kB gzipped):

```css
/* app.css; the app imports Shell, TextField, primitives/button and the charts package's Chart */
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/styles-base.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/sources/Shell.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/sources/TextField.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/sources/primitives/button.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-charts/sources/Chart.css';
@import '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/themes/paper.css';
```

A module the app starts importing needs its line too, or its classes are missing.

Components import by path, one module each:

```ts
import { DataTable } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/DataTable'
import { Button } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/primitives/button'
import { Chart } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui-charts/Chart'
```

Each package's `exports` map lists every path it offers and nothing else: a module it does not list is the library's own and cannot be imported. Every component exports the type of its props as `<Component>Props` from the same path (`import { DataTable, type DataTableProps } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/DataTable'`).

## The frame every app has

Every app stands in the same frame, so a person moving between apps finds everything in the same
place. It has four parts, and an app has all four from its first screen:

- **`Shell` with a `Rail`** of the app's places down the left; `markHref` makes the rail's mark a
  link home, and a collapsed rail expands from its mark or by pulling its edge. `TopBar` holds a
  search field at its start (`search={<SearchField .../>}`, which `/` focuses) and the palette's
  button at its end. A new `contentKey` on `Shell` mounts the page afresh, as after a reconnect.
- **The command palette**, always there: `Shell`'s `palette` takes its groups and opens it on ⌘K
  (Ctrl K off a Mac) and from `TopBar`'s button in the top right corner, which shows the key.
  `placeCommands` makes its "Go to" group from the rail's groups (an entry's `keywords` found but
  never drawn), and `appearanceCommands` its scheme, density and theme commands, from
  `useAppearance` or from an app's own look (`{ scheme, onSchemeChange, theme, onThemeChange }`),
  so an app's places and look come for free. `paletteFilter="terms"` wants every word typed to
  match, a label starting with it first. A screen adds its own groups while it is mounted with
  `useCommands(groups, deps)` from `hooks/use-commands`, placed by each group's `rank`; a command
  with a `detail` or `artwork` is a two-line row. A second ⌘K closes it; `paletteOpen` with
  `onPaletteOpenChange` holds it from outside, and `mayOpenPalette(over)`, asked first with the
  layer on top, refuses it over the app's own full-screen views or lets it replace the app's own
  search. `useShell()` from `Shell` gives a screen `openPalette` and `openShortcuts`.
- **Keys, one registry**: a screen binds its keys with `useShortcuts(bindings, deps)` from
  `hooks/use-shortcuts`, each `{ id, key, mod?, shift?, alt?, label?, group?, scope?, inFields?,
  inDialogs?, run }`, the key named by the character it types (`event.key`), so it works on any
  layout; quiet while typing in a field and while a dialog, a menu or the palette is open.
  `Shell`'s `shortcuts` (the keys the app answers itself, or `[]`) makes it hold the shortcuts
  dialog, opened on `?` and from the account menu, listing every bound key with a `label`;
  `shortcutsOpen` with `onShortcutsOpenChange` holds it from outside, for a palette row. Never
  add a `keydown` listener of the app's own for a shortcut. `useOverlay`, `useScrollMemory` and
  `useReducedMotion` (all in `hooks/`) give the app's own overlays, lists and motion the same.
- **An `AccountMenu`** in the rail's foot, always there, before the app has sign-in too: then it is
  `local`, named for the local user or "Local", with a neutral avatar, settings and appearance, and
  no sign-out (`onSignIn` offers Sign in there). The place is held, and the frame looks the same in
  every app. `scheme` with `onSchemeChange` puts Light, Dark and System in the menu itself, and
  `extra` adds the app's own rows, each `{ id, label, icon, onSelect }`.
- **A `StatusLine` as `Shell`'s `foot`**, the strip along the window's bottom edge: the connection
  or the server's state, the active model or project, background work, the version. With it, the
  `AccountMenu` sits in the bottom-left corner level with the strip, so the account and the status
  read as one bar across the window. An app without a foot looks unfinished.

In a desktop shell (Electron or Tauri) with the native title bar hidden, give `Shell` (and `SignIn`
or `AppBar`) `desktop`: the top strip becomes the window's drag region (`-webkit-app-region` for
Electron), `trafficLights: true` on macOS leaves room for the window's buttons, and where the
webview ignores `app-region` (Tauri on macOS) `onWindowDrag` and `onWindowZoom` call the app's own
window API, such as `getCurrentWindow().startDragging()`. `isDesktopShell()` in `lib/desktop` says
whether the page runs in one. The library never imports the shell.

On a phone the rail opens as a drawer, always drawn expanded. Pass `Shell` the router's location as
`route` (`route={location.pathname}`) so the drawer closes on any navigation, the palette's too;
`drawerOpen` with `onDrawerOpenChange` holds it. A state of the whole app, such as a server not
answering, goes in `Shell`'s `banner` as a `Banner`, between the top bar and the content. The shell
pads the safe-area insets itself; a home-screen web app sets `viewport-fit=cover` in its viewport
meta and adds no padding of its own.

The look is kept by `useAppearance`, called in the app's root: it reads the theme, scheme,
density, corners, typeface and motion from `localStorage`, follows the system's scheme until one is
chosen, and wears them on `<html>` (`data-theme`, `.dark`, `data-density`, `data-motion`, `--radius`
and the typeface variables). `ThemePicker` takes its settings and setter, with the option lists
`THEMES` (every theme in the tokens), `CORNERS` and `TYPEFACES` from `lib/appearance`. Every call
follows the same kept look, so a settings page calls `useAppearance()` again with the same defaults.

```tsx
import { AccountMenu } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/AccountMenu'
import { useAppearance } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/hooks/use-appearance'
import { CORNERS, THEMES, TYPEFACES } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/lib/appearance'
import { appearanceCommands, placeCommands } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/lib/commands'
import { Rail, type RailGroup } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/Rail'
import { SchemeToggle } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/SchemeToggle'
import { Shell } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/Shell'
import { StatusItem, StatusLine } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/StatusLine'
import { ThemePicker } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/ThemePicker'
import { TopBar } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/TopBar'

const PLACES: RailGroup[] = [
    { id: 'work', entries: [{ id: 'runs', label: 'Runs', icon: Play, href: '/runs' }] },
    { id: 'system', title: 'System', entries: [{ id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: Settings, href: '/settings' }] },
]

export function App() {
    const { settings, setSettings } = useAppearance()
    const navigate = useNavigate()
    return (
        <Shell
            palette={[...placeCommands(PLACES, navigate), ...appearanceCommands(settings, setSettings)]}
            rail={
                <Rail
                    mark={<Mark />}
                    name="Tidevann"
                    groups={PLACES}
                    foot={<AccountMenu name="Local" local onSettings={() => navigate('/settings')} onAppearance={() => navigate('/settings')} />}
                />
            }
            top={<TopBar trail={[{ label: 'Runs' }]} actions={<SchemeToggle />} />}
            foot={
                <StatusLine note="Connected to api.example.org">
                    <StatusItem label="project">harbor</StatusItem>
                    <StatusItem>1.4.0</StatusItem>
                </StatusLine>
            }
        >
            <Routes />
        </Shell>
    )
}

/** The settings page: the same kept look, in the picker. */
function Appearance() {
    const { settings, setSettings } = useAppearance()
    return <ThemePicker value={settings} onChange={setSettings} themes={THEMES} corners={CORNERS} typefaces={TYPEFACES} system />
}
```

An app with only a light and dark switch needs no more than `useScheme()`, which answers
`{ scheme, resolved, setScheme }` (light, dark or system, kept and worn as `.dark`), or
`SchemeToggle`, the theme toggle wired to it. `useAppearance(defaults)` takes the look an app starts
in until the person chooses, such as `{ theme: 'paper' }`; give `SchemeToggle` the same scheme as its
`fallback`.

So the page never shows the wrong scheme while it loads, `appearanceScript()` writes the kept look
on `<html>` before the page draws. A Vite app puts it at the top of `<head>`:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { appearanceScript } from '@winterop-com/sokkel-ui/lib/appearance'

const appearance = {
    name: 'appearance',
    transformIndexHtml: () => [{ tag: 'script', children: appearanceScript(), injectTo: 'head-prepend' as const }],
}
// plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), appearance]
```

An app rendered on a server puts `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: appearanceScript() }} />`
first in its `<head>`. Given the same defaults as `useAppearance`, it starts in the same look.

## Docs

- [Component index](https://github.com/winterop-com/sokkel-ui/blob/main/docs/components.md): every exported component by package and area, with its import path, what it is and a story that shows it
- [README](https://github.com/winterop-com/sokkel-ui/blob/main/README.md): what is in the library, install, styles, themes and optional peer dependencies
- [Charts](https://github.com/winterop-com/sokkel-ui/blob/main/docs/charts.md): how charts are drawn from rows, the kinds and the fields they read
- [Plan](https://github.com/winterop-com/sokkel-ui/blob/main/docs/plan.md): what the library holds and why
- [Storybook](https://winterop-com.github.io/sokkel-ui/): every component and composition, live

## Rules for an app

- Install the packages and never copy from them: no vendored component, no copied source, no local fork of a part.
- Check the component index before building any UI part. A part that exists is used as it is.
- A part an app needs to differ becomes an option in the library, never a local edit or a wrapper that patches it in the app.
- Complex parts belong in the library. Before building a complex custom component, ask whether it belongs in sokkel-ui instead. If it is a reusable part, not one screen's glue, it is added to the library as a component or an option on one, and the app uses that.
- Report what is missing. A missing feature, a missing option or a bug found while building an app is reported directly to sokkel-ui as an issue at https://github.com/winterop-com/sokkel-ui/issues. The library serves only its own apps, so the owner can add it quickly. Never work around it locally in the app.
